name: Shannon mathematical theory of communication
description: A mathematical theory treating source information, channel capacity and transmission under noise.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: Claude Shannon published the first part of A Mathematical Theory of Communication.

evidence.supports: Shannon identifies Nyquist and Hartley papers and extends the communication theory.

events.caveats: The second part appeared in October 1948; the publication does not prove implementation of later systems.

evidence.supports: Shannon identifies Nyquist and Hartley papers and extends the communication theory.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated episode established in cited evidence for this scope, not a global priority claim.

research.note: Independent reader: Checked Shannon’s 1948 opening and footnotes naming both Nyquist papers and the Hartley paper as his theoretical basis. Earlier named theoretical foundations now have sourced records and links.

links.statement: Shannon cited Nyquist’s April 1924 paper as a theoretical basis.

evidence.supports: Shannon names Nyquist’s two papers and Hartley’s paper as a basis of his theory.
